memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord came down in the cloud and stood there with him and proclaimed his name, the Lord. And he passed in front of Moses, proclaiming, 'The Lord, the Lord, the compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness, maintaining love to thousands, and forgiving wickedness, rebellion and sin.'" - Exod 34:5-7a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is God's own description of Himself, and it is worth reading slowly. Compassionate. Gracious. Slow to anger. Abounding in love and faithfulness. Forgiving wickedness, rebellion and sin.

Remember the setting. This comes immediately after the golden calf — after betrayal, idolatry and three thousand deaths. If ever there were a moment for God to define Himself by wrath, this was it.

Instead, when God announces His own name, mercy comes first and mercy dominates.

This passage becomes the most quoted description of God in the entire Old Testament. David sings it (Ps 103:8). Jonah complains about it (Jonah 4:2). Joel appeals to it (Joel 2:13). Israel returns to it again and again, because it is God's own testimony about Himself.

Notice the three words: wickedness, rebellion and sin. Deliberate evil, defiant revolt, and ordinary falling short. God covers all three categories. There is no sin in your life that falls outside this list.

And every attribute here reaches its clearest expression at the cross, where love and faithfulness met and God was shown to be both just and the justifier (Rom 3:26). If you want to know what God is like, this verse is His own answer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which word in God's self-description do you find hardest to believe?
2. How does it change things that God introduces Himself with mercy first?
3. What sin have you assumed is beyond His forgiveness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are compassionate, gracious, slow to anger and abounding in love. Help me believe that this is truly who You are toward me. Amen.
